title: Teleop episode QA: sync, frame gaps and task metrics
scenario: Validate robot teleop episodes (missing streams, too few frames, camera frame gaps, camera/joint sync within an inclusive 20 ms window), then report per-task success and recorded time and fleet-level tag/operator counts.

verified.why_correct: bisect_left returns the insertion point, so the closest sample is either just before it (i - 1) or at it (i). The bounds check handles t before the first or after the last sample, and `gap < best` is fine because equal gaps give the same distance either way.

bugs.title: Sync window excludes the 20 ms boundary
bugs.why: Rule 4 makes the 20 ms window inclusive. With `<`, the three EP-03 camera frames whose nearest joint sample is exactly 20 ms away (around the joint dropouts at 400, 1200 and 2000 ms) count as unsynced.
hints: EP-03 is reported at 0.95. Look at its joint stream around 400 ms: which sample is nearest to that camera frame?
Check how sync_ratio decides that a frame is synced against README rule 4.
probes: Why did EP-11, which sits right at the 0.9 threshold, keep its ratio?
Why does EP-03 stay valid with or without the fix?
bugs.symptom: test_1 test_sync_ratios: EP-03 shows sync_ratio 0.95 instead of 1.0 (it still counts as valid). Every other ratio matches.

bugs.title: fps counts frames instead of intervals
bugs.why: duration is measured first frame to last frame, which spans frames − 1 intervals. Dividing the frame count by it overstates the rate (60 frames over 2.36 s gives 25.42 instead of 25.0).
hints: A 40 ms camera should be exactly 25 fps. Why does EP-01 show more?
Look at how fps is derived from frames and duration in camera_stats.
probes: Why does the error shrink for longer episodes?
Why didn't this change any episode's validity?
bugs.symptom: test_1 test_frame_rates: every fps is a little too high (EP-01 25.42, EP-02 25.46, EP-05 23.58 ...) instead of 25.0 / 23.11 etc.

bugs.title: Any non-blank success string counts as a success
bugs.why: bool() of any non-empty string is True, so `false`, `False` and `No` are read as successes. Only the blank EP-09 cell stays False.
hints: pick shows a 1.0 success rate. Count the success column for the valid pick episodes.
Follow how the `success` cell becomes a bool.
parse_bool should return clean(value).lower() in TRUTHY.
probes: Why was wipe's success rate unaffected?
Which other values in this CSV would bool() get right by accident?
bugs.symptom: test_2 test_success_rates: pick 1.0 and pour 1.0 instead of 0.6 and 0.0; place and wipe unchanged.

bugs.title: Recorded time floored to whole seconds
bugs.why: `//` floors the millisecond total to whole seconds before rounding, so 11070 ms becomes 11 instead of 11.07. round() can't bring the lost fraction back.
hints: Every recorded_s value is a whole number. Is that plausible for 2.07 s episodes?
Look at the ms-to-seconds conversion in task_metrics.
probes: Why doesn't round(..., 2) rescue the value?
Where else in the code is milliseconds converted to seconds, and why is that one fine?
bugs.symptom: test_2 test_recorded_seconds: whole numbers {'pick': 11, 'place': 6, 'pour': 3, 'wipe': 3} instead of 11.07 / 6.12 / 3.5 / 3.94.

bugs.title: Blank tags split into an empty tag
bugs.old: return [tag.strip() for tag in text.split(";")] if text else []
bugs.why: `"".split(";")` is `[""]`, not `[]`, so the three blank-tag episodes get one empty-string tag. tag_counts gains `"": 3` and untagged comes back empty.
hints: Where does the empty-string key in tag_counts come from?
Look at what split_tags returns for a blank cell.
Return [] when the cleaned text is empty (`... if text else []`).
probes: Why did EP-07's single-space cell end up the same as the truly blank ones?
Would `if tag.strip()` inside the comprehension also work? Is it equivalent?
bugs.symptom: test_3 test_tag_counts: tag_counts has an extra '' key with count 3 (and untagged would be empty).

bugs.title: Operator counts include rejected episodes
bugs.old: operators = Counter(ep.operator for ep in valid)
bugs.new: operators = Counter(ep.operator for ep in episodes)
bugs.why: The counter runs over every episode instead of the valid subset, so the four rejected episodes are credited to alice, bob and carol.
hints: carol shows 3 episodes, but only one of hers is valid.
Compare which list each Counter in summarize iterates over.
probes: Why was dave's count right anyway?
Which summary field is meant to look at invalid episodes, and how does it get them?

context_qa.q: What is the flow inside build_report()?
context_qa.a: `load_episodes` reads episodes.csv into `Episode` objects, `load_streams` reads streams.json into `{episode_id: {sensor: sorted timestamps}}`, `evaluate_all` turns each episode into `EpisodeStats`, then `task_metrics` and `summarize` build the task table and the summary.

context_qa.q: How does load_streams key the streams?
context_qa.a: By `norm_episode(item["episode"])` (trim + upper-case) and then by the sensor name trimmed and lower-cased. Timestamps are converted to int and sorted.
The absolute distance in ms from `t` to the closest value in the sorted `samples` list, looking at the neighbours either side of the bisect insertion point. It returns None for an empty list.

context_qa.q: In what order does evaluate() check the rejection reasons?
context_qa.a: missing_stream (no camera or no joints), then too_short (`frames < MIN_FRAMES`, 20), then frame_gap (`max_gap > MAX_GAP_MS`, 150), then unsynced (`sync_ratio < MIN_SYNC_RATIO`, 0.9). If none match, `valid` is set to True.

context_qa.q: What does camera_stats return for a stream?
context_qa.a: A tuple `(frames, duration_ms, fps, max_gap)`: the count, last minus first timestamp, the computed frame rate rounded to 2 decimals and the largest consecutive difference. With fewer than 2 frames it returns `(frames, 0, None, None)`.

context_qa.q: Which episodes does task_metrics look at?
context_qa.a: Only episodes whose `stats[ep.id].valid` is True, grouped by `ep.task`. Tasks are emitted in sorted order.

context_qa.q: What data does summarize work from?
context_qa.a: It builds `valid` from the episodes list, then uses Counters for tags, operators and rejection reasons. The rejection Counter reads from `stats.values()` filtered to invalid ones.
